evidence.description: The actor declaration uses the open access modifier.

candidates.explanation: Swift actors do not support inheritance and cannot be declared open. This declaration is invalid Swift.
candidates.title: Invalid open actor declaration

evidence.description: The completion closure synchronously calls the actor-isolated track method.
The escaping completion is invoked directly inside a notification-settings callback, without returning to the analytics actor.

candidates.explanation: The completion carries actor-isolated work into an external escaping callback, but its plain closure type does not preserve an actor-executor requirement. Invoking it directly provides no guarantee that track executes on the Analytics actor, undermining the isolation protecting tracker state.
candidates.title: Actor-isolated tracking escapes through a callback

evidence.description: The instance-selection preference can be changed through a nonisolated setter.
Network configuration reads the mutable preference separately for endpoint selection and authentication-header selection.

candidates.explanation: The preference can change between the two reads because this factory and the setter are nonisolated. A configuration can therefore combine one endpoint selection with the other authentication decision, including attaching micro-instance credentials to the normal endpoint or omitting them from the micro endpoint.
candidates.title: Endpoint and authentication use inconsistent preference snapshots

evidence.description: The selected endpoint is force-unwrapped without a preceding validity check.

candidates.explanation: The selected endpoint is optional, but configuration construction unconditionally force-unwraps it. A nil endpoint causes a runtime trap during tracker creation rather than a handled configuration failure.
candidates.title: Tracker construction force-unwraps an optional endpoint

evidence.description: The common tracking path suppresses tracker calls when TESTING is defined.
The settings event calls tracker.track directly without the TESTING guard.

candidates.explanation: The direct settings-event path bypasses the test-build suppression implemented by the common tracking method. Consequently, TESTING does not consistently prevent events from being submitted to the tracker.
candidates.title: Settings tracking bypasses test-build suppression
